name: Mk3
summary: Same airframe as Mk2 with the recovery electronics reworked so the parachute cannot deploy late, and tougher fins.

parts.description: Tangent ogive nose cone, printed as a hollow shell with a shoulder that locates in the avionics bay. A removable ballast pocket lets the CG be trimmed.
Sealed bay for the flight data logger. The exposed band carries the static vent holes; the spigot is the friction-fit separation joint with the recovery tube.
Sealed bulkheads keep ejection gas away from the electronics and the barometer.
Removable sled holding the logger; slides out at the field for data download and battery changes.
Arduino Nano-size board running the data-logging firmware: fixed-rate logging, launch/apogee/landing detection and an altitude beep-out after landing.
parts.label: Flight data logger
parts.changeNote: New firmware: apogee is confirmed over several filtered readings, with a timer as a backup.

parts.description: Pressure sensor used for altitude. It reads the static pressure through the vent holes.
parts.changeNote: Moved away from the bulkhead and given its own vent, so bay pressure disturbances reach it less.

parts.description: Accelerometer (±16 g) and gyroscope, axes aligned with the rocket.
Sized for over an hour armed on the pad, strapped down for 15–20 g.
External switch so the logger can be armed on the pad without opening the bay.
parts.changeNote: Lets the electronics be armed on the pad, after the rocket is on the rail.

parts.description: Forward shock cord anchor through the aft bulkhead.
Upper body tube housing the parachute, shock cord and protector.
Links the nose/av-bay to the aft section after ejection.
Size to be set with the MATLAB simulator (target landing speed 6 m/s or less).
parts.label: Parachute

parts.description: Shields the parachute from the hot ejection charge gases.
parts.label: Chute protector

parts.description: Lower body tube with through-the-wall fin slots and rail button holes.
parts.label: Aft body tube

parts.description: 29 mm motor mount tube; carries thrust into the airframe.
Centres the motor tube in the body tube. The fin tabs are bonded between the two rings.
parts.label: Centring ring

parts.description: The motor pushes on this ring, so thrust goes into the motor tube rather than the motor sliding forward.
The motor has not been chosen yet. A 29 mm G-class dummy is shown for sizing, and its mass is an estimate.
parts.label: Motor (not chosen yet)

parts.description: Screw-on retainer so the ejection charge pushes the parachute out, not the motor.
Through-the-wall fins, to be sized for a 1–2 caliber stability margin.
parts.changeNote: Thickness up from 3 mm to 4.5 mm, with a glue fillet along each root.

parts.description: Guides the rocket along the launch rail until it is fast enough to be stable.
Aft shock cord attachment on the forward centring ring.

changes.title: Apogee detection that ignores a single bad reading
changes.detail: The firmware now filters the pressure signal and waits for several readings in a row to show descent before it fires.
changes.why: In Mk2 one disturbed reading delayed deployment by seconds. A filtered signal with a short confirmation window is far harder to fool.

changes.title: Backup deployment timer
changes.detail: A timer starts at launch detection and fires the parachute at a fixed time if nothing else has.
changes.why: Whatever happens to the sensors, the parachute still comes out.

changes.title: Thicker fins with root fillets
changes.detail: Fins are now 4.5 mm ply with an epoxy fillet along both sides of each root.
changes.why: The Mk2 fin split along the root on landing. More thickness and a fillet spread that load.

changes.title: Barometer relocated
changes.detail: The sensor sits mid-bay with its own static vent.
changes.why: It reads cleaner pressure, which makes the apogee decision easier in the first place.

changes.title: Arming switch added
changes.detail: A screw switch reachable from outside the airframe.
changes.why: The electronics stay off until the rocket is on the rail, which is safer and saves battery.

buildLog.title: Firmware rewrite started
buildLog.text: Replayed the Mk2 pressure log through the new apogee logic on the bench until it triggered within 0.3 s of the true peak.

buildLog.title: Deployment tests
buildLog.text: Five ground tests of the deployment charge with the new firmware and the backup timer. All five fired.

buildLog.title: Fins replaced
buildLog.text: Old fins cut out and 4.5 mm fins bonded in with fillets. Mass went up by 18 g, checked against the stability margin.

buildLog.title: Final assembly and balance
buildLog.text: Full stack assembled, armed and disarmed on a test rail. Centre of gravity re-measured with the heavier fins.

flights.title: Flight 1
flights.notes: Stable climb, parachute out within half a second of apogee, soft landing and no damage. Peak height was short of the 500 m target.
